items.abstract: <jats:p>Iterative improvements from feedback is a general approach for many, if not all, successful systems.Ground-truth-in-the-loop is critical.Language models (LMs) like ChatGPT are phenomenal, however, there are still issues like hallucinations and a lack of planning and controllability.We may leverage LMs' competence of language to handle tasks by prompting, fine-tuning, and augmenting with tools and APIs.AI aims for optimality.(Current) LMs are approximations, thus induce an LM-to-real gap. Our aim is to bridge such a gap.Previous study shows that grounding, agency and interaction are the cornerstone for sound and solid LMs.Iterative improvements from feedback is critical for further progress of LMs and reinforcement learning is a promising framework, although pre-training then fine-tuning is a popular approach.Iterative updates are too expensive for monolithic large LMs, thus smaller LMs are desirable.A modular architecture is thus preferred.These help make LMs adapt to humans, but not vice verse.We discuss challenges and opportunities, in particular, data & feedback, methodology, evaluation, interpretability, constraints and intelligence.</jats:p>
title: Iterative improvements from feedback for language models

items.abstract: Large Vision-Language Models have demonstrated remarkable capabilities in multimodal understanding, yet they face critical challenges in visual in-context learning, weak-to-strong generalization, and domain-specific reasoning. We propose RobustVLM, a unified framework that addresses these challenges through three complementary modules. First, Adaptive Visual Context Learning enables effective visual in-context learning through intent-aware demonstration retrieval, intent-oriented image summarization, and adaptive context aggregation, allowing models to leverage visual demonstrations without parameter updates. Second, Weak-to-Strong Robust Transfer facilitates robust generalization from weak supervision signals by dynamically adjusting supervision strength across capability dimensions and transferring adversarial robustness properties from weak to strong models. Third, Domain-Adaptive Abnormal Feedback improves domain-specific reasoning by constructing domain-aware abnormal feature banks and applying feedback loops that guide the model to focus on domain-critical features. Extensive experiments on six benchmarks spanning visual question answering, medical imaging, text retrieval, and general reasoning demonstrate that RobustVLM consistently outperforms existing methods, achieving improvements of 2.5 percent on TextVQA, 3.3 percent on VizWiz, 2.6 percent on VQA-RAD, 1.9 percent on SLAKE, 1.6 percent on MS MARCO, and 1.9 percent on MMLU compared to the strongest baselines. Ablation studies confirm the contribution of each module, and human evaluation shows that RobustVLM produces more accurate and relevant responses in the medical domain.
title: RobustVLM: Enhancing Large Vision-Language Models through Adaptive Visual Context Learning, Weak-to-Strong Robust Transfer, and Domain-Adaptive Feedback

items.abstract: <jats:p>Sequential manipulation planning has been a critical imperative to achieve a higher level of autonomy in robotics.  Classical approaches to address task planning problems are  based on symbolic formalisms, such as Planning Domain  Definition Language (PDDL) [1], and search for state transition plans to reach task goals. In practice, such task plans  are often programmed as Finite State Machines (FSMs),  which incorporate expert knowledge specifying control and  execution details. Due to its limitation of scalability [2],  Behavior trees (BTs), which represent policies in a state-less,  hierarchical tree structure, have gained increasing popularity  for complex task planning. Its advantages of modularity,  reusability and reactivity, make it a more desired formalism  for long-horizon manipulation tasks.</jats:p>
title: Behavior Tree Generation using Large Language Models for Sequential Manipulation Planning with Human Instructions and Feedback
